items.title: Charles "Creole Charlie" Levy Interview, 1962-01-03
items.q: So, um, this boy, Willie Jones and I, we sneaked down the district.

ctx.x: There weren't any jazz men around Chicago?

No, there weren't any then. They were all playing, they were all playing Scott Joplin Rags then. And, uh, Elger came from, up from New Orleans, and by knowing my mother from New Orleans, she came. And, uh, they said that Charles had started studying violin, but it didn't do no good. Maybe it was the teacher, or maybe it was him. And so, uh, they brought my violin out, and Elger said, my goodness, they said, man, shouldn't have had a full-size violin like that to teach you? He said, so I started taking lessons…
Was it mainly brass music, or did you hear violin music, too?
